title: Real origin browser implementation
objective: Replace localhost-rewritten website frames with isolated native browser surfaces loading real website origins through the application-private forward proxy.
constraints: Windows, Linux and macOS ship together; macOS 14 or newer is acceptable.
Linux X11/XWayland is explicitly approved. Select the GTK/X11 backend before toolkit initialization; native Wayland is not a release requirement for this host.
An engineering probe on one OS is not authorization for a single-platform release.
All website traffic must traverse the resolved application network path, including redirects, child frames, workers and WebSockets. Unsupported transports fail closed.
The proxy is private to the application, binds loopback on an OS-assigned port, requires native-held per-attempt authentication, and never falls back directly.
No localhost website aliases, TLS interception, fake browser identities, disabled web security, or privileged application IPC in remote pages.
Bind host, profile, proxy, connection and owner database to an immutable attempt. Stale callbacks never operate on a successor.
Browser-controlled HTTPS, certificates, cookies and storage replace page-side emulation.
Bundled Chromium is authorized; CEF is the selected feasibility candidate because public WebKit APIs did not establish the full containment contract.

Forced dark mode and automatic login remain active on authentication and challenge pages at the user's explicit request. CAPTCHA interaction is still human, and this does not grant new credential consent.
Website request permissions support shared website/domain defaults and per-connection overrides, explicitly confirmed by the user.
Provider acceptance is measured separately from transport and rendering correctness; Google may reject embedded sign-in independently.
Preserve existing unrelated pending changes. No production account operations are authorized by this implementation request.
The user explicitly chose local-only verification. Do not create a branch, commit, push or dispatch remote CI; unavailable Linux/macOS runners remain unverified.
For unsupported native HTTPS trust policies, the user chose guidance only. Keep saved and inherited trust policies unchanged; do not add a one-click strict-policy switch or automatic fallback.

ownership.main: Architecture, shared contracts, registration, integration, plan and final evidence
ownership.windows: Pinned native API feasibility and then assigned Windows host files
ownership.webkit: Linux and macOS feasibility and then assigned platform host files
ownership.verification: Independent loopback transport tests and adversarial acceptance fixtures

deliverables: Verify APIs against pinned Tauri/Wry and official browser sources.
Prove or reject native per-profile proxy authentication, request admission and non-proxy traffic containment on each OS.
Choose one host architecture; document engine packaging, sandbox, native-tab embedding and accessibility implications.
Produce a real-origin local browser probe, not another string-only readiness claim.
phases.gate: No readiness report until actual profile/proxy binding and native enforcement are installed before navigation.

deliverables: Reuse OriginBrowserSession and the private HTTP/CONNECT relay; keep target TLS opaque.
Resolve direct-upstream, configured HTTP/SOCKS, tunnel and chained paths explicitly. Reject unsupported paths without substituting direct.
Native-owned session registry and attempt-fenced create, navigate, cancel, close and failure lifecycle.
Exact-origin resource/redirect admission, separate from permission to release credentials.

Domain-level request permissions with explicit precedence, visible effective rules and per-request-class controls. Domain network grants never grant credentials, auto-login consent, certificate exceptions or privileged app access.
Endpoint-only proxy authentication; no proxy secrets in renderer messages, process arguments, URLs or logs.
Revoke admission and active streams on owner lock/close, host failure or proxy failure.
phases.gate: Loopback tests prove destination TLS identity, authentication isolation, unauthorized-host rejection, cancellation and no fallback.

deliverables: Isolated website surfaces with no privileged Tauri IPC or app-origin ancestor.
Profile allocation and cleanup tied to attempt; persistent login retention requires explicit database ownership and lock policy.
Native certificate verification and existing trust-policy integration; do not silently discard pins or exceptions.
Contain DNS prefetch, proxy bypass lists, loopback bypass, QUIC, WebRTC and unsupported socket APIs.
Treat startup settings, installed hooks, runtime failure handling and adversarial test evidence as separate readiness requirements.
Deny automatic popups, downloads, file access, external protocols and permission requests until their owned review paths exist.
phases.gate: Each platform passes the same native isolation and network-tripwire fixtures.

deliverables: Mount the native surface in the connection-tab viewport, handling bounds, zoom, DPI and window changes.
Synchronize native visibility with selected tab, menus, dialogs, trust prompts, database lock and detach/reattach.
Wire back, forward, reload, stop, address, title, loading and failure diagnostics using typed attempt-scoped events.
Keep URL display truthful; real-origin sessions never load a protected localhost website alias.
Bound event payloads and diagnostics; never include cookies, request bodies, authorization or query values.
Keep the old mediator an explicit legacy choice; a failed real-origin session must not silently switch engines or routes.
phases.gate: UI integration tests reject stale events; hidden views cannot receive input, and closed or owner-locked views cannot continue network activity.

deliverables: Origin-bound autofill and explicit submission consent using reviewed application adapters, not generic scripts in every frame.
Separate challenge interaction from auto-login; never solve or bypass a CAPTCHA automatically.
Keep forced dark mode and automatic login active on login/challenge pages; do not silently disable either as a compatibility fallback.
Use native pre-paint styling or engine dark rendering with narrowly scoped origin-bound login adapters; retire legacy URL/cookie/prototype shims, not the requested features.
Native dark background and theme readiness without leaving interactive invisible overlays.
Migrate dialogs, permissions, downloads, popups and external-link review without proxy bypass.
Remove obsolete cookie/URL/request shims only from the new host; preserve legacy mode until its consumers migrate.
phases.gate: Per-feature regressions cover manual login, staged login, consent, unrelated frames, verification prompts and cancellation.

deliverables: Local HTTPS fixture verifies location.origin, secure context, same-origin child frames and cross-origin isolation.
Native cookie, storage, redirect, module import, dedicated/shared/service worker and WebSocket tests where supported.
Independent local tripwires detect any direct connection, including loopback targets, after route loss and revocation.
Proxy credentials never satisfy a website authentication challenge.
Human-driven provider matrix: Google identifier-to-password transition, Cloudflare challenge, Porkbun sign-in, session reload and logout.
Report opening, form, password, challenge, authenticated and reload stages individually; a rendered form is not a passed login.
Repeat acceptance on Windows, Linux and macOS. No production credentials or profiles enter automated fixtures.
phases.gate: Transport, native-host, full-app and provider evidence are distinct and all required release checks are terminal.

deliverables: Package and sign native helpers/runtime resources on every supported platform and architecture.
If Chromium is bundled, pin matching runtime and bindings, preserve sandboxing, establish security-update and rollback procedures.
Add CI gates for native host contracts and packaging; keep unsupported/runtime-missing states explicit.
Enable the new production mode only once the cross-platform readiness contract is met.
Publish accurate configuration, migration and diagnostic documentation; record remaining provider limitations.
phases.gate: No platform-only rollout, unverified ready capability, silent downgrade or claimed provider guarantee.

domainPermissions.sharedScope: App-wide website/domain defaults for public request policy only; never store connection secrets or query values in shared rules.
domainPermissions.overrideScope: Each saved connection can inherit or explicitly override its website defaults, including destination rules.
precedence: Non-overridable native safety and route constraints
domainPermissions.matching: Exact canonical HTTPS origins initially, grouped and labelled by domain. No inferred wildcard/subdomain/port grants. Any later subdomain rule requires explicit opt-in and public-suffix validation.
ui: Connection Internal proxy controls: inherit/override and destination rules
Blocked-request review: display effective rule and offer explicitly scoped changes
safety: Network grants never authorize credential forwarding, login submission or certificate exceptions
Inline/eval execution settings belong to the owning document, not an unknown destination grant
Existing sessions receive an explicit apply/reload choice; stale attempts cannot acquire new permissions
Show the matching source and precedence of every effective setting
domainPermissions.status: Strict shared/per-connection policy models, persistence normalization, themed editor and matching Rust engine implemented and unit-tested. Native CEF browser/context callbacks consume one immutable policy snapshot, classify requests using native metadata and intersect grants with session admission; unknown classes deny. Shared and per-connection editors are mounted. Native authority derives immutable saved-owner policy snapshots; legacy sessions do not consume this new policy. Operational admission now requires successful native global/system policy installation and readback; policy loss permanently revokes admission for the process. Live containment acceptance remains unverified.

dataPath: Remote website top-level native Chromium document at its actual HTTPS origin
Attempt-private browser profile and authenticated fixed proxy
Application-private HTTP/CONNECT relay with destination admission
Explicitly resolved connection network path: direct upstream, proxy, SSH tunnel or chain
Original website, with browser-to-website TLS kept end to end
controlPath: Trusted app shell issues bounded commands with database, connection, tab and attempt identity
Native session owner validates the unlocked owner, consent and current attempt
Native host performs the action and returns redacted typed status events
Remote documents never receive the app's invoke handler, database APIs or relay secrets

engineDecision.candidate: CEF bundled Chromium; feasibility, not production availability
engineDecision.reason: Public WKWebView APIs inspected did not establish complete HTTP(S)/worker/socket admission and WebRTC containment. Use a common engine if it can satisfy the contract on all three platforms.
engineDecision.bindingEvaluated: cef and cef-dll-sys pinned together at 154.3.0+154.0.32 behind sorng-browser-host's cef-host feature and the root application's native-browser feature. Normal full-feature development and release selections include native-browser. Startup admission uses checked native policy installation, not a hardcoded enabled or disabled value. Operational admission does not attest cross-platform production acceptance.

platformFindings.windows: Raw WebView2 can prove first real-origin transport behavior in a native child; supported WebView2 flags alone are insufficient evidence for all-traffic containment.
platformFindings.macos: CEF requires CefAppProtocol/CrAppControlProtocol integration into NSApplication, preserving Tao event handling and termination. A pinned Tao patch or explicit runtime bridge needs runtime validation.
platformFindings.linux: Inspected CEF native child path accepts an X11 parent. XWayland also requires the app GTK shell to use X11. The user approved X11/XWayland; native Wayland is rejected explicitly before creating a child, not silently converted after initialization.

mustProve: macOS framework/helper bootstrap before app services, then a checked event-dispatch bridge on the existing TaoApp before CEF initialization
Linux native child embedding and supported X11/Wayland session behavior
Windows sandbox-enabled bootstrap, native child lifecycle and helper process packaging
No traffic bypass with fixed proxy, worker/resource interception and alternative-transport restrictions
No browser engine initialized inside the privileged app webview's JavaScript context
notAssumed: CEF installation alone makes Google accept embedded sign-in
A proxy preference alone contains every browser transport
An off-screen canvas preserves IME, accessibility, clipboard or focus without additional host work
Separate browser windows are an acceptable substitute for connection tabs

workPackages.acceptance: All five public-API tests pass. These are Rust clients, not native browser acceptance.

workPackages.acceptance: Website 401, stale attempt, wrong endpoint/realm/scheme and revocation never invoke the credential callback.

workPackages.output: First real native-browser HTTPS probe through the private relay using disposable storage and synthetic local certificates.
workPackages.acceptance: Real HTTPS location, top-level document, secure context, native cookies/storage and no app IPC. Passed on Windows WebView2 146.0.3856.84. Wry's inert ipc property still exists but no IPC handler is installed and native messaging/host objects are disabled. No production Ready report or public-site login claim.

workPackages.output: Implemented shared single-thread external message pump and native bootstrap providers for Windows sandbox bootstrap DLL entry, Linux X11/XWayland, and macOS 14+ TaoApp event bridge and sandbox-first helper loading. Root app entry, setup, UI pump and shutdown are wired behind native-browser. Windows feature-enabled app library and dedicated helper compile. Genuine Windows and WSL2 Linux x64 entry probes pass without initializing a browser. Linux CEF initialization/rendering, macOS execution and native ARM64 execution remain unverified.
workPackages.acceptance: Public API/native lifecycle proof on macOS and Linux; any app-shell or off-screen rendering expansion is called out before implementation.

workPackages.output: Native host crate implements isolated CEF context proxy preparation, auth/request guards with immutable domain permissions, owned and borrowed platform child descriptors, hidden child creation, navigation/control, redacted sequenced events and close/crash relay revocation. App-owned registry, typed command registration, native database ownership and runtime startup are wired. Saved proxy-only chains resolve from the owning protected profile and are registered at startup; unsupported SSH/VPN paths reject rather than borrowing active ports or falling back directly. Operational admission waits for actual native policy installation/readback. Revocation is terminal, while a fenced cleanup pump can drain closing windows. Certificate features without native translations still reject. Complete containment acceptance is not established.
workPackages.acceptance: Actual browser processes start sandboxed, bind to the correct route/profile, deny unsupported capabilities and shut down without affecting other tabs.

workPackages.output: Built and tested typed native transport, attempt-fenced controller and native viewport with bounds, tab/modal visibility, focus revision, late-create cleanup and owner-lock handling. Engine selection lives only in Settings, not a tab selector bar. An absent preference defaults to real-origin; explicitly saved legacy preferences remain unchanged. Browser controls, capability notice, engine preferences and shared/per-connection permission editors use the app's semantic theme, native tooltips, spacing and dialog components. Owner-only address-bar events retain complete validated URLs while diagnostics remain redacted. Native command registration and saved database-owner proof are wired. Actual cross-platform native tab behavior remains unverified and the production readiness gate remains closed; a default preference does not bypass it or silently substitute legacy mode.
workPackages.acceptance: No silent legacy/direct fallback; resizing, tab switches, modals, detached windows and reconnects preserve owner/attempt and input isolation.

workPackages.output: CEF forced-dark startup flags, renderer feature handshake and origin-bound manual/generic/Porkbun/Google/Exchange ECP/Exchange OWA/Vodafone Smart Router adapters are implemented with native and DOM fixture tests. Google identifier and password stages have separate native delivery fences. The root bridge now obtains fresh native consent per attempt, binds exact origins and submission rights for ten minutes, resolves credentials only from the saved owning database and revokes on owner/attempt loss. Consent is never inferred from a renderer grant ID. Other saved application adapters or custom selectors still reject unless manual login is explicitly selected. Actual native delivery, first-paint darkness, UA/client-hint coherence and live provider acceptance remain unverified.
workPackages.acceptance: No white first paint or silent feature suspension, no repeated form submission loops, no secrets in unrelated frames, and no production URL/cookie/prototype rewriting in new mode.

workPackages.output: Expanded deterministic gate to native viewport/controller and domain policy tests. Six-platform CEF package/acceptance workflow is authored but will not run remotely under the user's local-only instruction. Windows packaged run17 completes generic and Google-shaped staged synthetic login, real secure top-level HTTPS, native cookies and isolated child frames. Cookie/storage isolation and clean closure of three fixture attempts are observed, with no post-revoke requests. Native zoom/find calls succeed before revocation and reject afterward. The same-ID browser replacement cleanup bug was repaired without loosening credential guards. Aggregate acceptance remains failed because native first-paint pixels and DNS/socket containment are not fully verified; actual Google/Cloudflare acceptance and Linux/macOS runtime execution remain unproved.
workPackages.acceptance: Denials are observed at destination listeners, not only JavaScript errors. Missing runtimes/platform runs remain not-run; provider failures stay failures.

workPackages.output: Offline package verifier covers Windows/Linux/macOS x64 and ARM64, exact runtime/binding pins, sandbox ABI, complete resources/locales/framework/helper layouts and staged byte identity. All six downloaded archives now match their pinned strong digests. A Windows client package and isolated app-entry/bootstrap probe were produced locally; Windows and WSL2 Linux x64 entry probes pass, while actual packaged browser acceptance still fails. Reverse-DNS executable names and macOS dotted names are preserved; build-local acquisition remains strictly offline. Whole-matrix assessment rejects Windows-only or duplicate reports. Normal app dev/release packaging still needs its CEF-aware driver. Linux/macOS browser initialization, signatures/notarization and full-platform release acceptance remain outstanding.
workPackages.acceptance: Packaged artifacts, not dev-only binaries, pass the same gates before the real-origin mode reports production readiness.

riskControls.risk: Provider rejects an embedded browser even at its real origin
riskControls.control: Record Google password-stage and Cloudflare human-challenge results; never promise acceptance or spoof browser identity.

riskControls.risk: Dark extension or auto-submit changes sensitive page behavior
riskControls.control: Keep both active as requested. Test stage-specific timing and scoped DOM changes; report incompatibility rather than silently disabling features.

riskControls.risk: Opaque HTTPS prevents proxy-side content inspection
riskControls.control: Move certificate trust, URL admission, request controls and extensions to trusted native engine boundaries; do not reintroduce TLS interception.

riskControls.risk: Persistent Chromium profiles retain database secrets after lock
riskControls.control: Default to attempt-private storage; explicit retained profiles need owner-bound retention, cleanup, lock and at-rest protection design before enabling.

riskControls.risk: CEF subprocess sandbox or engine version drifts
riskControls.control: Pin matching runtime/bindings, validate package manifests and sandbox startup, and treat security updates as a maintained release dependency.

riskControls.risk: Native views cover application menus or capture input when hidden
riskControls.control: Native visibility and focus ownership follow tab/modal lifecycle; exercise DPI, detach/reattach and accessibility.

riskControls.risk: App-private endpoints are reachable from website traffic
riskControls.control: Never grant privileged app endpoints; authenticate the relay independently and restrict target admission before opening any socket.
